title: High Strength and Fracture Resistance of Reduced-Activity W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr High-Entropy Alloy for Fusion Energy Applications

questions.broad: For structural materials intended for fusion plasma-facing components, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness, and why? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to an unperturbed baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an outcome that would falsify it.
questions.problem_constrained: For an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy made from low-activation refractory elements, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations expected relative to pure tungsten, the applicable boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.
questions.expert_context: Earlier W-based high-entropy alloys showed promising microstructural stability, high-temperature strength, and irradiation tolerance, but most contained Nb, Mo, Cr, or Ni, whose activation behavior and other service limitations restrict their suitability for plasma-facing components. Candidate structural materials must combine thermal and mechanical performance with low neutron activation and rapid radioactive decay. The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy uses refractory, relatively low-activation constituents and has shown creep and molten-salt-corrosion resistance, yet its plastic strain and toughness remain unreported and poorly understood. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to pure tungsten, the boundaries of validity, the cited prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an observation that would falsify it.
